items.title: 75230_Howard McGhee oral history interview
items.q: Yeah, we could hear Earl Hines and so forth on the radio. ... I used to listen to Earl Hines and Fletcher Henderson and all the bands that played in the Grand Terrace.

ctx.x: Yeah, Silver's Resort. J.R. got the gig out there to replace them. So when I got out there, I saw these guys, and I knew these guys could play, you know, because I had heard them play in Shawnee, Oklahoma one night in a dance, and I'd heard the Gray Brothers, and I know that Jay can play -- so I wanted to be with him. So I told him. He said, "Well, we got another job we're going on to, so why don't you come on and go with us."

In the meantime, Watts had me and a guitar and a drum and himself, and I said, "Well, I can't learn anything just the way they're playing, because I was teaching them" -- because I'm there. It's better I go where I can learn something, and I want to know... I asked Jay would he teach me how to write for the group, so he said "Yeah." So we had two trumpets and a tenor and a bass and drums and a singer; he had Bill Powell. So I learned a whole lot from Jay, like all the tunes Earl Hines was playing -- "Deep Forest"…
